# Fairstay PropCo Bookkeeping (`fairstay-propco-bookkeeping`)

Property company bookkeeping for nursing-home real estate: rent unpaid or short, escalators not billed, operator rent coverage and occupancy below the lease minimums, operator financials overdue and leases ending. Lease numbers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay PropCo Bookkeeping never sends default notices or letters to an operator.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-propco-bookkeeping demo
npx -y fairstay-propco-bookkeeping mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Three fictional leases reviewed on 20 April 2026. Planted:

- L-40021 (Cedar Hollow): the 2.5% escalator stepped up in April, but April was billed at the old rent.
- L-40022 (Willow Bend): March was paid short and April is unpaid. Rent coverage is 1.02x against 1.2x, occupancy is 72% against 75%, and the lease ends 31 December.
- L-40023 (Pecan Grove): operator financials for February were due 45 days after month end and have not arrived.

Lease numbers are in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `propco_check` | Check rent, escalators, operator coverage and reporting for each lease. | runs |
| `propco_write_report` | Write propco.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and propco.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/propco). | runs |
| `propco_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `propco_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `propco_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `propco_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `default_notice_send` | Fairstay PropCo Bookkeeping never sends default notices or letters to an operator. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `propco_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `leases` (required) | Leases under --root: lease number, operator, facility, start, end, base monthly rent, escalator percent, minimum rent coverage and occupancy, days to deliver financials, rent due day |
| `rent` (required) | Rent roll under --root: lease, month, billed, paid, paid date |
| `financials` | Operator monthly financials under --root: lease, month, EBITDAR, rent, occupancy |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: ending_warn_days |
| `as_of` | Review date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-propco-bookkeeping inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Leases (`leases`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `lease_no` (required) | text (masked) | Lease, Lease #, Lease Number, Lease ID, Agreement |
| `operator` (required) | text | Operator, Tenant, Lessee |
| `facility` | text | Facility, Property, Building |
| `start` | date | Start, Commencement, Start Date |
| `end` | date | End, Expiration, End Date, Term End |
| `base_rent` (required) | amount | Base Rent, Monthly Rent, Initial Rent |
| `escalator_pct` | number | Escalator, Escalator %, Annual Increase |
| `min_coverage` | number | Min Coverage, Rent Coverage Covenant, Coverage Minimum |
| `min_occupancy` | number | Min Occupancy, Occupancy Covenant |
| `financials_days` | number | Financials Days, Reporting Days, Financials Due Days |
| `rent_due_day` | number | Rent Due Day, Due Day |

### Rent roll (`rent`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `lease_no` (required) | text (masked) | Lease, Lease #, Lease Number, Lease ID, Agreement |
| `period` (required) | text | Period, Month, Rent Month |
| `billed` | amount | Billed, Rent Billed, Charged, Invoice Amount |
| `paid` | amount | Paid, Received, Amount Paid, Collected |
| `paid_on` | date | Paid On, Received On, Payment Date |

### Operator financials (`financials`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `lease_no` (required) | text (masked) | Lease, Lease #, Lease Number, Lease ID, Agreement |
| `period` (required) | text | Period, Month, Rent Month |
| `ebitdar` | amount | EBITDAR, EBITDARM |
| `rent` | amount | Rent, Rent Expense |
| `occupancy` | number | Occupancy, Occupancy %, Occ % |
| `received_on` | date | Received On, Received, Delivered |

## Settings file (`propco_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ending_warn_days` | Flag leases ending within this many days (default 365) |

## Memory

`propco_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `propco_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `lease_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-propco-bookkeeping": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-propco-bookkeeping",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-propco-bookkeeping -- npx -y fairstay-propco-bookkeeping mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-propco-bookkeeping tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-propco-bookkeeping sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-propco-bookkeeping inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-propco-bookkeeping call propco_check '{"leases":"<leases>","rent":"<rent>"}'
fairstay-propco-bookkeeping eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-propco-bookkeeping demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
